questions: Did you remain conscious and aware throughout the fall?
Did you experience a sudden loss of muscle strength immediately before falling?
Did you have any warning symptoms such as dizziness, light-headedness, palpitations, or visual dimming?
Did anyone observe jerking movements, stiffening, tongue-biting, or loss of bladder control?
Have you had similar sudden falls repeatedly?
Do these falls occur only when someone is watching or accompanying you?
Were you able to get up and walk normally soon afterward?
Are the attacks triggered by laughter, surprise, anger, embarrassment, or other strong emotions?
Do you have excessive daytime sleepiness or irresistible episodes of falling asleep?
Have you experienced sleep paralysis or vivid dream-like hallucinations when falling asleep or waking?
Do you have sudden episodes of weakness involving the face, jaw, speech, or neck?
Does the weakness resolve completely within a few minutes?
Have you ever had a stroke, spinal cord disease, or progressive neurological illness?
orders: Full neurological examination, including gait, tone, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination, and examination for functional signs (Hoover sign, inconsistency, and distractibility).
Twelve-lead ECG and supine and standing blood pressure and pulse measurements.
Serum glucose, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and creatine kinase obtained during or immediately after an episode.
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side)
entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm)
co-activation sign on passive movement of the affected limb
'whack-a-mole' sign (restrain the affected limb and watch the others)
anticipatory jerk to a feigned tendon-hammer approach (Hallett sign)
suggestibility / sham stimulus (tuning fork or vibration applied as 'treatment')
variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination
gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards)
observation for excessive slowness or uneconomic posture
MRC power in all four limbs
